headline: High-risk shared git and filesystem overlap: semantica can ingest Aider’s edits and both can mutate the same repo, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and semantica ingests local files, web pages, and git repositories. That creates a default path where semantica can consume Aider-authored content as input. The shared repo is documented, but there is no provenance isolation or parser hardening shown, so injection is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF semantica ingests Aider-authored repo files as instructions or metadata, injection risk is present.
IF the shared git repo contains attacker-controlled text, semantica may parse it as trusted content.
mitigations: Separate Aider and semantica into different repos.
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents in semantica.
Add provenance tags to repo-derived inputs.
Review any semantica parser that treats markdown, comments, or YAML as directives.
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization before semantica consumes repo files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, secrets, and many file types. Both have filesystem access and broad write/read paths, so a shared workspace can expose sensitive material from one agent to the other. Because semantica also handles tokens, passwords, and private keys, the blast radius includes direct exfiltration or accidental disclosure.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace or repo, sensitive files can be read by both.
IF semantica is pointed at a directory containing secrets or enterprise documents, those contents may flow into its outputs.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and mount only least-privilege paths.
Remove secrets from any shared repo before running either agent.
Restrict semantica to a read-only sanitized dataset.
Rotate any credentials present in shared directories.
requires-engineering: add OS-level isolation between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state. Aider explicitly shares state via a shared git repo, while semantica supports git repositories and a shared intelligence layer. Without locking, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt branch history, and the conflict is dangerous by default in a shared repo workflow.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git branch or working tree, race conditions can overwrite changes.
IF either agent auto-commits without coordination, history corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use a lock file or external mutex around git operations.
Review diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared repo writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code edits and git commits, and semantica is built around decision records, provenance, and downstream data workflows. If semantica treats Aider’s output as authoritative, an incorrect edit can propagate into structured records or automated actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the default path can cascade errors across work products.
conditions: IF semantica ingests Aider-generated diffs or summaries without verification, errors can propagate.
IF semantica uses Aider output to update decision records or APIs, downstream impact becomes broader.
mitigations: Require human review before semantica acts on Aider output.
Compare Aider output against source files before ingestion.
Limit semantica to read-only analysis of Aider changes.
Log provenance for every derived record.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between Aider and semantica.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is documented as handling source code and git history, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and secrets. If those data classes are co-located, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the pair. The profiles do not show a shared compliance regime, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF enterprise data or secrets are stored in the same workspace as source code, retention obligations may conflict.
IF semantica processes regulated records while Aider logs or commits them, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Set explicit retention rules for each workspace.
Redact secrets before Aider edits files.
Document which agent may process which data class.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
